verdict.summary: You create an OAuth 'public connection' yourself in the Notion Developer portal, and the docs say you can use it without a Marketplace listing. Notion's security review and listing review apply only if you want to appear on the Marketplace. One thing is unclear: the docs say the Authorization URL field only fills in after you submit for review, so test early to confirm installs work before you submit.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min (plus a few hours if you also prepare a Marketplace listing)
verdict.approval_wait: none for OAuth use; 5-10 business days for the optional Marketplace listing response

gates.name: Public connection in your development workspace
gates.unlocks: You can run the OAuth flow with your own client ID and secret and connect your own Notion workspace.
limits: Installation scope (Any workspace vs Selected workspaces only) is permanent once set
The Authorization URL field in the Configuration tab only fills in after you submit for review, so you may need to build the authorize URL yourself
If you change capabilities later, users must re-authenticate

gates.name: Unlisted public connection (Selected workspaces only, or Any workspace without a listing)
gates.unlocks: Other users can authorize the connection. Each user goes through OAuth and the page picker on their own.
limits: No install cap, user cap or test-user allowlist appears in the pages read
'Selected workspaces only' limits installs to the workspaces you pick at creation, and those connections can't be listed on the Marketplace
Enterprise workspaces may only allow approved connections, and an admin must install it once before approving it
Rate limits: 180 requests/min per connection (600 on Business/Enterprise workspaces), about 3 requests/s for data-source queries

gates.name: Any-workspace connection, optionally listed on the Notion Marketplace
gates.unlocks: Any Notion workspace can install the connection through OAuth. A Marketplace listing also makes it discoverable in Notion.
limits: Notion security review and listing review are needed only for a Marketplace listing
Only 'Any workspace' connections can be listed
Listings can be rejected over brand/trademark issues, quality concerns or baseline criteria, and you can resubmit
gates.time_to_reach: Immediately for unlisted OAuth use; about 5-10 business days for a Marketplace listing response

steps.title: Choose the installation scope
steps.detail: Decide between 'Any workspace' (any workspace can install, and it can be listed on the Marketplace) and 'Selected workspaces only' (only workspaces you pick, never listable). For an agent product used by outside customers, pick Any workspace.
gotchas: You can't change the scope after creation. To switch, you have to create a new connection.

steps.title: Create the public connection
steps.detail: Sign in to the Notion Developer portal. In the sidebar's Build section, select Public connections and click Create new connection. Enter a connection name and choose your development workspace.
gotchas: The portal only works with JavaScript enabled, so you have to do this in a browser.

steps.title: Set the redirect URI and capabilities
steps.detail: In the creation form, add the redirect URI and choose capabilities. Content can be read, update or insert. Comments can be read or insert. User information can be none, without emails, or with emails. Ask only for what your agent needs.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

values.label: Installation scope
values.value: Any workspace (or Selected workspaces only, per step 1)

gotchas: Per a community guide, redirect URIs can't contain fragments, relative paths or wildcards, and can't be a public IP address.
If you add more than one redirect URI, the token request must include redirect_uri.
Fewer capabilities make workspace admins more likely to approve the install. Changing capabilities later forces users to re-authenticate.

steps.title: Fill in company and legal details
steps.detail: An agent can draft the tagline, privacy policy and terms of use. You then host them and enter the company name, website, privacy policy URL, terms of use URL and support email. Community sources say these are required for public connections and show up on the authentication screen.
gotchas: This list comes from community sources that may be out of date. Notion's official docs don't list these fields.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and secret
steps.detail: After creating the connection, open its Configuration tab and copy the OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret. Store the secret somewhere secure.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config with your credentials
steps.detail: In Composio, create an auth config for the notion toolkit using OAuth2 with your own client ID and secret. Leave scopes empty, because Notion uses capabilities instead of scope strings. Make sure the Composio callback URL shown there exactly matches the redirect URI you set in Notion.

steps.title: Test the authorization with your own workspace
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio, or open the authorize URL with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and owner=user. Pick pages in the page picker and approve. Then check that the token exchange returns an access_token and refresh_token, and that an API call works.
gotchas: The Configuration tab's Authorization URL field stays empty until you submit for review. Build the URL yourself and check that installs work before you submit.
Each refresh returns a new refresh token. Always store the latest one.
Notion-Version header: the latest version listed is 2026-03-11.

steps.title: Optionally add a template page
steps.detail: To duplicate a starter page into each user's workspace when they authorize, paste a public Notion page URL into 'Notion URL for optional template' on the Configuration tab.

steps.title: Onboard other users and workspaces
steps.detail: Send users through the Composio connect flow. Each user authorizes on their own and picks which pages to share. For Enterprise customers that only allow approved connections, an admin has to install the connection once and then approve it for the workspace.

steps.title: Prepare the Marketplace listing (optional)
steps.detail: Only needed if you want to be discoverable on the Notion Marketplace. Draft the name, description, category, tags, images and logo, and link the listing to your Any-workspace public connection.
gotchas: Avoid using Notion's brand or trademarks in your name or assets. That's a common reason for rejection.

steps.title: Submit the listing for security and listing review
steps.detail: Submit the listing from the Developer portal. Notion runs a security review on public connections before listing them.

steps.title: Wait for Notion's response and resubmit if needed
steps.detail: Notion says it responds by email within 5-10 business days. If they request changes, make them and resubmit.

requirements.item: Connection name, development workspace, redirect URI(s), installation scope, capabilities
requirements.detail: Required fields in the public connection creation form.

requirements.item: Company name, website, privacy policy, terms of use, support email, tagline
requirements.detail: Community sources say these are required for public connections and appear on the auth screen. Notion's official docs don't confirm this.
Needed to be listed on the Marketplace. You choose it at creation and can't change it.

requirements.item: Listing assets: name, description, category, tags, images, logo
requirements.detail: Needed only for a Marketplace listing.
Needed before a Marketplace listing, not for OAuth use.

scopes.effect: Set on the connection, not requested as OAuth scopes. Users also limit access to the pages they pick in the page picker. Changing capabilities forces users to re-authenticate.
Optional. Leave off unless your agent reads or writes comments, since fewer capabilities make admins more likely to approve.

scopes.scope: User information (none / without emails / with emails)
scopes.effect: 'With emails' gives access to user email addresses. Ask for the lowest level that works.

blockers.symptom: No Authorization URL appears in the connection's Configuration tab
blockers.cause: Notion only fills in this field after the public connection is submitted for review.
blockers.fix: Build the authorize URL yourself (client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, owner=user) or let Composio generate it. If installs fail before submission, submit for review.

blockers.symptom: You want to list on the Marketplace but listing isn't allowed
blockers.cause: The connection was created with 'Selected workspaces only', and the scope can't be changed.
blockers.fix: Create a new public connection with 'Any workspace' and move users to the new client ID.

blockers.symptom: Enterprise users can't install the connection
blockers.cause: The workspace only allows approved connections.
blockers.fix: Ask a workspace owner or admin to install it once and then approve it for the workspace.

blockers.cause: Brand or trademark issues, quality concerns, or not meeting baseline criteria.
blockers.fix: Make the requested changes and resubmit.
blockers.contact: Notion replies to listing submissions by email

blockers.symptom: Token refresh fails after it worked once
blockers.cause: Each refresh returns a new refresh token, and the old one was reused.
blockers.fix: Save the new refresh_token from every refresh response.

composio.note: Composio offers managed OAuth2 for Notion, so you can start there with no setup. Scopes are empty because Notion uses connection capabilities and the page picker instead of scope strings. Register your own public connection if you want your own name, logo and capabilities on the consent screen, your own rate-limit budget per connection, a template page, or a Marketplace listing. Put Composio's callback URL from your auth config in the connection's redirect URIs.

evidence.claim: The developer portal for public connections is at app.notion.com/developers/connections and requires JavaScript.
evidence.quote: Notion JavaScript must be enabled in order to use Notion.

evidence.claim: Create a public connection via Build > Public connections > Create new connection.
evidence.quote: In the **Build** section of the sidebar, select **Public connections**.

evidence.claim: The creation form asks for name, development workspace, redirect URIs, installation scope and capabilities.
evidence.quote: Connection name and development workspace

evidence.claim: Installation scope is Any workspace or Selected workspaces only, and can't be changed after creation.
evidence.quote: Installation scope is set once, at creation time, and can't be changed afterward.

evidence.claim: The client ID and secret are in the Configuration tab.
evidence.quote: visit the **Configuration** tab to retrieve your **OAuth client ID** and **OAuth client secret**

evidence.claim: The Authorization URL field only fills in after submission for review.
evidence.quote: The Authorization URL field populates after a public connection is submitted for review

evidence.claim: The authorize URL needs client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and owner=user.
evidence.quote: Always use `user`.

evidence.claim: With multiple redirect URIs, redirect_uri is required in the token request.
evidence.quote: If there are more than one redirect URIs included in your connection settings, this field is required.

evidence.claim: Redirect URIs can't contain fragments, relative paths or wildcards, or be a public IP.
evidence.quote: It can't contain URL fragments, relative paths or wildcards, and can't be a public IP address.

evidence.claim: The code is exchanged at https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token using HTTP Basic auth.
evidence.quote: Send the `code` as part of a `POST` request to Notion's token endpoint

evidence.claim: The token response includes access_token and refresh_token plus workspace fields.
evidence.quote: The `refresh_token` will be used to refresh the access token, which generates a new `access_token`.

evidence.claim: Each refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token.
evidence.quote: Refreshes an access token, generating a new access token and new refresh token

evidence.claim: Users must re-authenticate when capabilities change.
evidence.quote: users will need to re-authenticate with a connection if the capabilities are changed

evidence.claim: Notion uses capabilities instead of OAuth scope strings.
evidence.quote: In general, you want to request minimum capabilities that your connection needs in order to function.

evidence.claim: Fewer capabilities make admin installs more likely.
evidence.quote: The fewer capabilities you request, the more likely a workspace admin will be able to install your connection.

evidence.claim: Each user authorizes on their own and picks pages.
evidence.quote: each user needs to complete the authorization flow individually.

evidence.claim: An optional template page URL can be set in the Configuration tab.
evidence.quote: add the URL of the Notion page you selected to the **Notion URL for optional template** input.

evidence.claim: Only Any-workspace connections can be listed. A listing needs name, description, category, tags, images and logo.
evidence.quote: Only public connections with an installation scope of **Any workspace** can be listed on the Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Notion responds to listing submissions within 5-10 business days.
evidence.quote: expect to hear back from our team within 5-10 business days via email.

evidence.claim: Rejection reasons include brand/trademark and quality, and you can resubmit.
evidence.quote: Connections are rejected for various reasons, from brand/trademark issues to quality concerns

evidence.claim: A public connection can be used without listing it.
evidence.quote: You can create and use a public connection without listing it.

evidence.claim: The security review is required before a Marketplace listing.
evidence.quote: Public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed on the Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Community: the public integration form requires tagline, privacy policy, terms, support email, company name and website.
evidence.quote: All these fields are required because you're about to create a public integration available to all Notion users.

evidence.claim: Community: the website and other details appear on the integration page and auth screens.
evidence.quote: Used to link to your integration's website or homepage in your integration page and authentication screens.

evidence.claim: Rate limit is 600 req/min per connection on Business/Enterprise and 180 on other plans.
evidence.quote: Business and Enterprise | 600 requests per minute

evidence.claim: Data-source queries are limited to about 3 req/s per connection.
evidence.quote: has a separate limit of about 3 requests per second per connection.

evidence.claim: The Overview page gives no install cap, user cap or dev-mode restriction for unreviewed connections.
evidence.quote: Public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed on the Marketplace.

evidence.claim: No install or test-user cap is stated for unlisted connections. Scope only limits which workspaces can install.
evidence.quote: Only the workspaces you select at creation time.

evidence.claim: There is no separate rate-limit tier for unreviewed connections.
evidence.quote: In the future, Notion plans to adjust rate limits to balance for demand and reliability.

evidence.claim: Enterprise workspaces can restrict members to approved connections.
evidence.quote: Approved only: Workspace members can only install connections pre-approved by a workspace owner.

evidence.claim: On Enterprise, an admin must install a connection once before approving it.
evidence.quote: Before you can approve a connection for the rest of your workspace, you or another admin will have to install it first!

evidence.claim: The latest Notion-Version is 2026-03-11.
evidence.quote: The latest version is `2026-03-11`.

open_questions: Can an Any-workspace public connection be installed by other workspaces before you submit it for review? The Authorization URL field only fills in after submission.
Does creating a public connection need a paid plan, workspace-owner role or business verification? The docs only say workspace owners are required for internal connections.
Do unlisted public connections have any install cap or user cap? None was found.
What exactly does the Marketplace review check, and what does the security review involve (questionnaire, depth)?
How long do access tokens last? Not stated.
Does Composio's managed Notion app need your own registration? Composio's default redirect is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add; confirm the exact callback in your auth config.
Are the company/legal fields (privacy policy, terms, support email) still required in the current portal? This comes only from community sources that may be out of date.
